summary: Mountaineer Cobbleflint guards the southern tower in the Valley of Kings, desperately seeking aid against the encroaching Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's military stretched thin across distant fronts, the defense of Loch Modan's southern passes falls to passing Alliance volunteers.

sections.title: A Thin Line in the Valley of Kings
sections.body: The massive dwarven monuments carved into the mountains of the Valley of Kings loom over a garrison under severe strain. Mountaineer Cobbleflint and his fellow guards stationed at the southern watchtower face an ever-growing invasion of troggs erupting from the rock. With much of King Magni Bronzebeard's regular army dispatched abroad to support Alliance commitments, the home front relies heavily on local patrols and hired blades to prevent the province from being overrun.

sections.title: The Stonesplinter Incursion
sections.body: The subterranean threat originates within Stonesplinter Valley, a craggy ravine carving into the southern peaks of Loch Modan. Troggs and their scouts have burrowed surface-ward in massive numbers, carving out fortified camps along the valley floor. Left unchecked, their scouting parties threaten the critical roads connecting Loch Modan to the southern passes, forcing the Mountaineers to wage a continuous war of attrition.

faq.q: Why is the garrison in Loch Modan so undermanned?
faq.answer: King Magni Bronzebeard has committed large portions of Ironforge's military to distant Alliance battlefields and outposts across Azeroth. This foreign commitment leaves home territories like Loch Modan protected primarily by light patrols of Mountaineers who must call upon traveling adventurers to stem regional invasions.

Mountaineer Cobbleflint is a dwarven sentry posted at the southern guard tower in the Valley of Kings. He coordinates perimeter security along the southern boundary of Loch Modan and directs counterattacks against the nesting trogg tribes.

Stonesplinter Valley lies south of Thelsamar, accessed by an entrance near the main road before reaching the massive dwarven statues in the Valley of Kings. The troggs maintain several encampments along its rocky floor.

faq.q: What makes troggs such a severe threat to the dwarves?
faq.answer: Troggs are aggressive, subterranean brutes that tunnel through solid rock, bypassing conventional surface walls and fortifications. Because they can erupt without warning beneath roads, settlements, and mines, dwarven authorities view their unchecked proliferation as an existential danger to Ironforge's security.

faq.q: Who do I speak to after helping Cobbleflint?
faq.answer: After thinning the ranks of the Stonesplinter troggs and scouts, Cobbleflint directs you to Mountaineer Gravelgaw, stationed just inside the adjacent watchtower, who manages the next phase of the patrol along the valley front.

While primitive, the Stonesplinter clan demonstrates rudimentary organization by deploying specialized scouts to reconnoiter the roads alongside brutish foot soldiers who maintain defensive camps throughout the ravine.

angles.text: For dwarven adventurers, answering Cobbleflint's call is a vital matter of homeland defense, ensuring that King Magni's ancestral valleys do not fall to subterranean pests while the army fights elsewhere.
Helping secure the Valley of Kings demonstrates the strength of the Alliance bond, answering Ironforge's plea when dwarven troops are deployed on distant allied fronts.
The crags and outcroppings of Stonesplinter Valley provide ideal terrain to pick off aggressive trogg sentries and scouting parties from high vantages.
